question: Why did Tor withdraw the newly revealed cover of This Crown Will Not Rule Me?

rungs.question: Why did Tor withdraw the cover?
rungs.answer: Tor learned generative AI had been used to make the art. Its own policies and its contracts with cover artists forbid that, and the authors' publishing contract also has a no-AI clause, so Tor took the cover down and said the imagery would not appear on any finished book.

evidence.quote: We have a no-AI clause in our contract. Tor also has a no-AI clause in their art contracts.
noting that its existing policies and contracts with cover artists prohibit the use of generative AI

counter.text: A December 2022 post quoting the authors says they once commissioned a Midjourney image for Magic Tides, shown only on their site: "we do not feel comfortable using the AI images commercially". Their line then was commercial use, not any use.

rungs.question: Why did Tor find out only after the cover was revealed?
rungs.answer: Readers spotted possible AI elements once the cover was public and said so, including in Instagram comments from two named artists. The authors passed this to Tor and asked for proof the art was human-made; Tor then confirmed AI had been used.

evidence.quote: Their feedback alerted us to this issue.
After readers raised concerns about the cover when it was revealed, the authors notified Tor and requested proof that the artwork was created by a human.

counter.text: none found, within the authors' post, the PW report and the 2022 Goodreads post; Tor's own Instagram statement would not load with its text.

rungs.question: Why did the review before the reveal not catch it?
rungs.answer: The checks rested on sketches and on whether the artist could make revisions. Tor commissioned the cover and a sketch reached the art department that looked like a normal cover sketch. The authors say they lack the expertise to spot AI art. Tor calls it a breakdown in its review process.

evidence.quote: In this case, the cover was commissioned by our publisher, and a sketch was provided to the art department. It looked like a typical cover sketch.
"Tor takes full responsibility for the breakdown in our review process," the publisher said

counter.text: PW reports earlier cases at Tor: reader criticism in February 2024 of AI stock images on a Bramble cover, and criticism in 2022 of the Fractal Noise cover, which used an AI-generated image. That points to a recurring gap rather than a one-off lapse.

rungs.question: Why did the no-AI clauses not stop it happening?
rungs.answer: The sources point to the clauses resting on the artist's word and reputation, checked against work that can look normal at sketch stage. The authors' response is to ask for project files and judge each artwork, which implies the clause alone gave no way to verify.

evidence.quote: We can no longer vet the artist. We have to vet every individual painting.
intend to review individual artworks rather than relying on an artist's reputation or assurances

counter.text: none found, within the three sources read; neither Tor nor the authors say how the AI use was finally confirmed.

rungs.question: Why did the artist use generative AI despite the contract?
rungs.answer: Nothing read answers this. The authors say they do not know the artist's circumstances, and Tor did not respond to PW's request for further comment.

evidence.quote: We don’t know what was going on that person’s life or what led to this unfortunate incident.
The publisher did not respond to requests for further comment.

counter.text: none found, within the three sources read.

landing.shows: Two contracts banned generative AI, yet the cover got through because review relied on sketches and trust in the artist. It was caught only once readers and artists looked at the public cover. Tor took the blame, and the authors moved from trusting the artist to checking each painting, perhaps by asking for project files.
landing.open_question: If a no-AI clause can only be checked by asking for each artist's project files, what does the clause itself guarantee?
